## Packages

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(janitor)
library(here)

raw_dir <- here("input", "raw")
processed_dir <- here("input", "processed")
output_dir <- here("output")
```

### Python

```python
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

raw_dir = Path("input/raw")
processed_dir = Path("input/processed")
output_dir = Path("output")
```
::::

## Import

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
# CSV
df <- readr::read_csv(
  file.path(raw_dir, "population_communes_2024.csv"),
  na = c("", "NA", "N/A")
)

# Semicolon-delimited CSV with decimal commas
df <- readr::read_csv2(file.path(raw_dir, "survey_results.csv"))

# Excel: inspect sheets before selecting one
readxl::excel_sheets(file.path(raw_dir, "source_workbook.xlsx"))
df <- readxl::read_excel(
  file.path(raw_dir, "source_workbook.xlsx"),
  sheet = "Data",
  na = c("", "NA")
)

# JSON; inspect the returned structure before assuming it is tabular
json <- jsonlite::fromJSON(
  file.path(raw_dir, "api_response.json"),
  simplifyDataFrame = TRUE
)
df <- json$data
```

### Python

```python
# CSV
df = pd.read_csv(
    raw_dir / "population_communes_2024.csv",
    na_values=["", "NA", "N/A"],
)

# Semicolon-delimited CSV with decimal commas
df = pd.read_csv(raw_dir / "survey_results.csv", sep=";", decimal=",")

# Excel: inspect sheets before selecting one
with pd.ExcelFile(raw_dir / "source_workbook.xlsx") as workbook:
    print(workbook.sheet_names)
    df = pd.read_excel(workbook, sheet_name="Data")

# JSON records; use json_normalize for nested objects
payload = json.loads((raw_dir / "api_response.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
df = pd.json_normalize(payload["data"])
```
::::

## Initial inspection

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
df <- df |> janitor::clean_names()

dplyr::glimpse(df)
dim(df)

missing <- df |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_missing") |>
  mutate(pct_missing = n_missing / nrow(df)) |>
  arrange(desc(pct_missing))

duplicate_rows <- sum(duplicated(df))
duplicate_keys <- df |> count(municipality_id, year) |> filter(n > 1)
```

### Python

```python
df.columns = (
    df.columns.str.strip()
    .str.lower()
    .str.replace(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", regex=True)
    .str.strip("_")
)

df.info()
df.shape

missing = (
    pd.DataFrame({"n_missing": df.isna().sum(), "pct_missing": df.isna().mean()})
    .sort_values("pct_missing", ascending=False)
)

duplicate_rows = df.duplicated().sum()
duplicate_keys = (
    df.groupby(["municipality_id", "year"], dropna=False)
    .size()
    .rename("n")
    .loc[lambda x: x > 1]
)
```
::::

## Unique and categorical values

Inspect known categorical and discrete identifier fields explicitly. Do not enumerate every value of continuous numeric columns.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
df |> count(region, sort = TRUE)
df |> distinct(year) |> arrange(year)

df |>
  summarise(across(c(region, status, year), n_distinct)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_unique")
```

### Python

```python
df["region"].value_counts(dropna=False)
df["year"].drop_duplicates().sort_values().tolist()
df[["region", "status", "year"]].nunique(dropna=False).sort_values()
```
::::

## Transform

### Rows, columns and types

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
df_selected <- df |>
  filter(year >= 2020, !is.na(value)) |>
  select(municipality_id, year, region, value) |>
  rename(bfs_code = municipality_id) |>
  mutate(
    bfs_code = as.integer(bfs_code),
    region = recode(region, "Lake Region" = "Lakes"),
    value_per_1000 = value / population * 1000
  )
```

### Python

```python
df_selected = (
    df.loc[(df["year"] >= 2020) & df["value"].notna(),
           ["municipality_id", "year", "region", "value", "population"]]
    .rename(columns={"municipality_id": "bfs_code"})
    .assign(
        bfs_code=lambda x: x["bfs_code"].astype("Int64"),
        region=lambda x: x["region"].replace({"Lake Region": "Lakes"}),
        value_per_1000=lambda x: x["value"] / x["population"] * 1000,
    )
)
```
::::

### Group and summarise

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
summary_df <- df |>
  group_by(year, region) |>
  summarise(
    observations = n(),
    total = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### Python

```python
summary_df = (
    df.groupby(["year", "region"], dropna=False)
    .agg(
        observations=("value", "size"),
        total=("value", "sum"),
        mean=("value", "mean"),
        median=("value", "median"),
    )
    .reset_index()
)
```
::::

### Reshape

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
df_long <- df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(population, households),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  )

df_wide <- df_long |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = value)
```

### Python

```python
df_long = df.melt(
    id_vars=["municipality_id", "year"],
    value_vars=["population", "households"],
    var_name="measure",
    value_name="value",
)

df_wide = df_long.pivot(
    index=["municipality_id", "year"],
    columns="measure",
    values="value",
).reset_index()
df_wide.columns.name = None
```
::::

### Join

Check key uniqueness and row counts before and after a join.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
stopifnot(nrow(lookup) == nrow(distinct(lookup, municipality_id)))

n_before <- nrow(df)
df_joined <- df |> left_join(lookup, by = "municipality_id")
stopifnot(nrow(df_joined) == n_before)

unmatched <- df |> anti_join(lookup, by = "municipality_id")
```

### Python

```python
if lookup["municipality_id"].duplicated().any():
    raise ValueError("lookup key is not unique")

df_joined = df.merge(
    lookup,
    on="municipality_id",
    how="left",
    validate="many_to_one",
    indicator=True,
)
unmatched = df_joined.loc[df_joined["_merge"] == "left_only"]
df_joined = df_joined.drop(columns="_merge")
```
::::

### Dates

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
df <- df |>
  mutate(
    reference_date = lubridate::ymd(reference_date),
    year = lubridate::year(reference_date),
    month = lubridate::floor_date(reference_date, "month")
  )
```

### Python

```python
df["reference_date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["reference_date"], errors="raise")
df["year"] = df["reference_date"].dt.year
df["month"] = df["reference_date"].dt.to_period("M").dt.to_timestamp()
```
::::

## Export

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
readr::write_csv(df, file.path(processed_dir, "population_communes_2024_clean.csv"), na = "")
writexl::write_xlsx(df, file.path(output_dir, "population_communes_2024.xlsx"))
arrow::write_parquet(df, file.path(processed_dir, "population_communes_2024.parquet"))
```

### Python

```python
df.to_csv(processed_dir / "population_communes_2024_clean.csv", index=False)
df.to_excel(output_dir / "population_communes_2024.xlsx", index=False)
df.to_parquet(processed_dir / "population_communes_2024.parquet", index=False)
```
::::

Excel and Parquet require their respective optional packages. Use CSV for broad interchange and Parquet when preserving types and efficient reuse matter.
